title: Masked Snapshot Service: versioned redactable transforms for analytics retention
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a Masked Snapshot Service (MSS) that produces point-in-time analytics snapshots with PII masked according to versioned transform rules. MSS enables: 1) creation of retention-compliant snapshots for downstream analytics and lookbacks, 2) audited, reversible masking operations for safe rollback during investigation, and 3) integration with legal-hold overrides and KMS-backed tokenization. The goal is to reduce blast radius of deletion backfills and give CS/SRE a fast way to provide redacted exports to customers and legal teams without full pipeline replay.
acceptance_criteria: MSS can produce a snapshot for a requested time range with configured transform version (v1, v2, ...) applied
Snapshots include an immutable manifest containing transform version, provenance hashes, and KMS key ID for tokenized fields
System supports a reversible masking mode: tokenization that can be re-identified by authorized service with audit trail
Snapshots can be served to downstream analytics jobs via S3 path with ACLs and a one-click revoke operation
Runbook for legal-hold override is documented and tested in staging (playbook + RBAC checks)
End-to-end tests cover schema-evolution (new fields), showing transforms skip/identity-preserve unknown fields without failing ingestion
work_notes: 2025-01-24: Spike completed comparing two approaches: (A) streaming transform during ingest vs (B) snapshot-time transform. We selected snapshot-time transforms to avoid double-writing and to allow rapid rule iteration.
Decision: use versioned transform manifests stored in Git (immutable tags) and referenced by manifest hash in snapshot metadata to enable reproducible replays and audits.
Trade-off: snapshot-time transforms add CPU overhead at snapshot creation. Mitigation: incremental snapshots + worker autoscaling and optional incremental masking cache keyed by record fingerprint.
Security: tokenization will use envelope encryption with KMS per-customer key; plan drafted with Security for key rotation implications on re-identification.

Data retention: snapshots inherit dataset retention policy; deletion of source data must trigger an expirable snapshot flag and optional redaction cascade to remove snapshot or irreversibly redact tokenized values.
Perf note: initial benchmarks show v1 transform on 1M events takes ~12m on a 16-core worker; we will add batching and vectorized masking kernels in follow-up iteration.
Integration: coordinate with console ACLs team for snapshot access flow and with billing to ensure snapshot egress is tracked.
Next: implement manifest store + CLI to create snapshot with chosen transform version; add manifests to repo under privacy-transforms/ and enforce signed commits.
Follow-up: design a small 'attestation export' JSON that auditors can use to verify transform version, manifest hash, and KMS key ID without exposing raw data.
Open question: whether reversible tokenization should require two-person approval in production — security to advise by 2025-02-20.
